newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ABORTION SEEN FREE FOR WOMEN WITH NO MEDICAL AID.
newsitem.headline: ABORTION SEEN FREE FOR WOMEN WITH NO MEDICAL AID.

text.p: Abortions should be free at state hospitals for South African women who do not belong to a medical aid scheme, a senior health official said on Thursday.

Health Department Director General Olive Shisana told a parliamentary committee debating new laws on the contentious issue that abortions should fall under the free healthcare provided to pregnant women by the state -- mostly the poor.
If a woman had a private medical aid scheme, however, the normal rates for comparative surgery would apply according to a scale of benefits.
Shisana said there were no apparent reasons for medical aid schemes to object.
"We envisage that medical aid should be able to pay for terminations of pregnancy because it's like any other health condition for a woman.
"We see no reasons why medical aid should not pay. If medical aids felt uncomfortable about this proposal, I believe they would have come (to parliament) to raise their concerns."

Parliament's portfolio committee on health concluded three days of public hearings on Wednesday and MPs have begun their deliberations on the draft law, which allows abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy.
